newsitem.title: USA: US corp debt issuance seen building, junk's up too.
newsitem.headline: US corp debt issuance seen building, junk's up too.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds issuance could easily see a repeat of Thursday's quick marketing of nearly $2 billion in supply, although no issues were firmly scheduled at mid-morning Friday, syndicate officials said.
Meanwhile, the junk bond issue calendar has rapidly grown with about $2 billion expected to price next week.

Back in high-grades, strong markets for Thursday's big investment firm deals and a rallying Treasury market may encourage opportunistic issuers to market. If not on Friday, they may aim for early next week ahead of the $3 billion Norfolk Southern Corp issue, one trader said.

"The market is pretty attractive because we haven't seen these (Treasury) rates in a few weeks," said one syndicate official at a New York investment firm. "Come next week you could see bad data, Norfolk Southern is going to price, so people are taking advantage of the dip in rates."

Reflecting positive sentiments on Friday, Lehman Brothers Holdings's $400 million seven-year deal and Salomon Inc's $500 five-year deal both tightened in spread when freed. Lehman's issue tightened two basis points to a 76 basis point spread; the Salomon notes tightened one basis point to a 73 basis point spread.

The Treasury market on Friday rallied on perceived bond-friendly comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan at a speech in New York on Thursday. Analysts said the Street was lowering odds of a Fed rate hike at the May 20 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee.

Turning to high-yield issues, one junk bond trader reported active bidding on Friday, sparked by the strong Treasury market and news of a $1.34 billion influx of cash to junk bond mutual funds in the latest week. Offerings were far fewer, though, and actual volume was termed light to moderate.

Cityscape Financial Corp issued $300 million 12.75 percent seven-year senior notes at par to yield 606 basis points over the curve. The issue, rated B1 and single-B, was priced through a CIBC Wood Gundy Securities syndicate.
Price talk on the issue widenened first to 12.50 percent and then to 12.75 percent from an initial 11.50 percent, according to a buyside source.
The issue was seen trading near 101 near mid-session.
Elsewhere, Therma-Wave Inc is expected to formally price its $115 million seven-year senior note issue on Friday via BT Securities Corp.
Street optimism was brimming over prospects for new issues next week given the AMG cash flow data.

Some of the larger deals include $470 million four-year zero coupon debt from Coleman Escrow Corp, earmarked to refinance outstanding zeros and convertible notes, and $400 million 10-year senior notes from Williams Scotsman.

The Williams Scotsman deal is part of a recapitalization following a buyout of the company by The Cypress Group and Keystone Inc. The company is the nation's second-largest lessor of mobile office units.
